goal: Sign the Electron Windows ARM64 build using a real ARM64-capable Windows signing toolchain or a supported non-ARM64 signing environment.
must_include: Identifies that electron-builder's `winCodeSign-2.6.0` cache contains `windows-10\x64\signtool.exe` but not the `windows-10\arm64\signtool.exe` path requested on Windows ARM64.

Recommends pre-populating/replacing the cached `windows-10` signing-tool contents with matching ARM64 SignTool files from an installed Windows SDK, or using an x64 Windows signing runner until upstream toolsets include ARM64.
Adds or verifies SHA-256 signing configuration if SignTool reports a missing file digest algorithm, for example `signingHashAlgorithms: ["sha256"]` under the Windows signing config.
Keeps certificate material in environment variables or the Windows certificate store rather than committing a `.pfx` and password.
must_not: Renames the x64 folder to `arm64` as a permanent production fix without noting that the binaries are the wrong architecture.
Disables signing for the ARM64 artifact and treats it as equivalent to signed x64 releases.
Changes the app target back to x64 while claiming an ARM64 package was produced.
acceptable_alternatives: Build the ARM64 package on ARM64 but perform signing on an x64 Windows host if the artifacts can be transferred safely.
Use Azure Trusted Signing or another electron-builder-supported signing backend when it works on the chosen runner.
Use an upstream electron-builder toolset release that provides ARM64 Windows signing binaries.
solved: The answer either supplies a correct ARM64 signing-tool cache/toolset or moves signing to a supported host/backend while still producing a signed ARM64 Windows artifact.
partial: The answer notices the missing ARM64 `signtool.exe` but proposes only a brittle folder rename or disables signing.
notes: Another writer covers .NET/MSIX ARM64; this scenario is intentionally Electron ARM64 signing.
